findings.title: 0247's watermark join adds a clock read to a trigger body that a separate structural census still asserts is clock-free, leaving two x42 cells genuinely red on this branch
findings.failure_scenario: packages/db/tests/x42-s5-helpers.mjs's FA_ACQUISITION_0216_CLOCK_NAMES roster states in prose that clara._tf_fa_acquisition_birth 'copies columns and takes its dates from the entry it fires for' and therefore carries no clock, and two tests (tests/x42b2-r7-s5-clock.test.mjs, tests/x42b2-s5c-clock.test.mjs) re-derive that roster from the live catalog and diff it against a pinned round-8 measurement. 0247's new join predicate calls now() (via coalesce(new.approved_at, now())), which is a clock read the roster's own text says this function does not have. Re-run independently on clara_l04 with the full gate chain: BOTH cells are red, and the actual-vs-expected diff is exactly the one name _tf_fa_acquisition_birth. This is a real, currently-failing pair of tests on the integration branch, caused by ticket #972's own migration -- not a Windows-only or CI-only red, and not fixed by any of the five lane-04 tickets.
findings.required_fix: Not owed by #972 itself (its own AC never mentions x42, and widening scope to fix another ticket's files is exactly what WORK-ORDER rule 5 forbids), and it IS disclosed: #977's report names it explicitly as follow-up #0 ('It is #972's file and #972's migration, so I left it alone -- but it is a lane red, not a Windows-only one, and the integrator will hit it'), with the one-line fix already identified (add _tf_fa_acquisition_birth to the bare-token roster and correct the comment in x42-s5-helpers.mjs). #979's report does not re-mention it. The integrator should either file this as its own ticket before merge or fold the one-line roster/comment fix into whichever ticket lands next, so the wave's own db suite is not carrying two known-red cells into integration without a tracking issue.

findings.title: Three near-identical single-name cohort blocks were added to rig-meta.mjs, one per migration, following the file's own pre-existing repeated idiom
findings.failure_scenario: The same four-line shape (a one-element UNGRANTED_FNS const, a COHORT export spreading it, and a matching `if (liveNames...) failures.push(...cohortFailures(...))` block in grantMatrixFailures()) is repeated three times across #973/#976/#977's commits for a single new function name each time. In isolation this reads as Duplicated Code / a Repeated Switch a shared helper (e.g. a `singleFunctionCohort(name, label)` factory) could collapse. No live risk: this is not a diff-introduced pattern -- the same file already carries this exact idiom for FA_DEPRECIATION_0227_COHORT, ACCRUAL_ADJUSTMENTS_0222_COHORT, and a dozen others predating this lane, and each report explains, correctly, why folding a new bimodal name into an OLDER cohort would be wrong rather than merely redundant (cohortFailures() fails a partial cohort by design).
findings.required_fix: None required -- this is the repo's own established convention (a documented-by-precedent repo standard under WORK-ORDER rule 4, which overrides the baseline smell here), not a violation this lane introduced. Flagged only as a judgement call for a future, repo-wide refactor of rig-meta.mjs's cohort machinery, out of scope for any single ticket.

summary: Five tickets (#972, #973, #976, #977, #979), fourteen commits, five new migrations (0247-0251), all independently re-verified on the lane rig: every re-run test file (21 individual cells across fa-birth-watermark, fa-depreciation-leg-fold, fa-particulars-completion-fold, authority-ref-human-instruction and fa-authority-retired-read) passed exactly as each report claimed, and operation-census/rig-isolation passed with only the one RIG.md-documented reset-gated skip. Every migration follows house law in full: a redo-tolerant prestate measuring live sha256(prosrc)/ACL/constraint text off the catalog (never transcribed from file text), set role clara_fn_owner/reset role around every recut body, a tail that re-derives every claim from the catalog rather than trusting the prestate, a preintegration gate module registered at the sorted (migration-order) position in packages/db/package.json's test chain, and a rig-meta.mjs cohort entry (or an explicit, precedented NO-COHORT record for #979) for every new ungranted internal. No applied migration, PRD, ARCHITECTURE or frozen-workflow file was touched; no new relation was created, so the FORCE RLS house rule does not apply. TDD discipline holds at the commit level: vertical-slice by vertical-slice, with documented red-for-the-right-reason and genuinely-run vacuity controls in every report (including a real mistake caught mid-ticket in #973 -- two invisible runtime splices lost on the first hand-recut, caught by the regression suite and restored, and disclosed rather than hidden). Every seam tested is either a real human door driven as a real persona session or a brand-new ungranted internal core the ticket's own brief names as a Key interface with no persona door to reach it instead. One MAJOR finding, independently confirmed by re-running the cells myself: #972's migration adds a clock read to a trigger body a separate structural census (x42's bare-token roster) still asserts is clock-free, leaving two tests genuinely red on this branch -- disclosed by #977's report as an unfixed follow-up (correctly out of scope for both tickets) but not yet tracked as its own item, and worth the integrator's attention before merge. Two NOTE-level, non-blocking findings: an uneven CI-lint-variant disclosure across the lane's own reports that resolves to the same pre-existing residue a sibling lane already flagged; and a small, precedented Duplicated-Code judgement call in three new rig-meta.mjs cohort blocks that mirrors the file's own established convention rather than introducing a new one.
